purpose: Accept registration transactionally and return a neutral verification-pending result without authenticating a browser session.

implementation_revision.semantics: Registration semantics remain unchanged. Shared Identity, Account, Token and Communications source hashes now bind the WELL-17 additions; the primary-email-change and recovery capabilities are documented separately. This is not an independent merge certification.

collaborating_domains.ownership: MessageIntent, protected envelope and nonce reservation; registration establishes intent, not delivery.
Registration evidence obligation and initial materialization schedule.

ash.caller_boundary: Internal transactional action. Application callers use Identity.register/1.
Private Account creation from the acceptance action; not a browser API.
AshAuthentication token resource; JWT issuance remains inside owner acceptance.

arguments: Atom-keyed map: operation_id UUIDv4, first_name, surname, email, password, preferred_language (en/af atom or string), confirmed_age_18? true, terms_version_id, privacy_version_id.
Nonblank names, nonempty password, accepted canonical mailbox and exact configured development legal versions are required.
returns: {:ok, %RegistrationResult{status: :verification_pending, account_id: UUID | nil, verification_proof: token | nil}}
Ordinary failure paths include {:error, :invalid_registration} and {:error, :registration_unavailable}; unexpected exceptions are not universally caught.
side_effects: New acceptance commits Account/credential/PMR/verification Token/operation plus Communications intent/envelope and Audit obligation/schedule in one Ash transaction.
Exact replay repeats no acceptance writes and returns no proof. Duplicate canonical email creates only a neutral operation binding.
No provider I/O or authenticated browser session.
caller_constraints: Never log or expose the transient verification_proof to browser callers.
Purpose-bound internal authorize?: false calls do not grant a general authorization bypass.

request_flow.summary: RegistrationController.create/2 validates browser input, then calls Identity.register/1; response is neutral and creates no session.
Identity checks operation replay, validates admission and allocates PMR; internal accept_registration action owns the source transaction.
AcceptRegistration.run/3 creates Account, verification challenge, Communications intent, Audit obligation/schedule, then binds operation.
Commit returns verification_pending; email delivery and verification consumption are separate capabilities.

states: unrecorded (request phase, not a persisted enum)

transitions.from_state: unrecorded (request phase, not a persisted enum)
guards: Validated immutable request, UUIDv4, legal/content/key eligibility and successful transaction.
Uniqueness arbitrates email, PMR and operation ID.
side_effects: Commit acceptance write set, or neutral duplicate-email binding.

guards: Before 24-hour expiry; same HMAC-bound input and matching password verifier; required old keys/provider supported.
side_effects: Return previous result with nil verification_proof; do not repeat acceptance.

guards: Operation expiry; replay independently rejects expired operations even before sweep.
side_effects: Clear replay/binding/result material, preserve operation UUID reservation; background expiry works in bounded batches.

security_invariants.summary: Identity owns Account, credential, PMR, verification challenge and registration operation; cross-Domain consequences use owning interfaces.
Neutral duplicate-email result must not reveal whether an Account exists; password and transient token are sensitive.
Development legal/browser fixtures are not production legal or release approval.

concurrency.summary: PostgreSQL unique identities arbitrate concurrent email/PMR/operation acceptance; process-local memory is not authority.
PMR collision retries allocation up to five attempts; email collision binds neutral result; operation collision rereads/replays.

idempotency_retry.summary: Exact immutable replay requires request fingerprint and slow password verifier; changed payload, key loss, expiry or tombstone refuses.
Do not retry by inventing new operation IDs to bypass expired or contradictory binding.

failure_recovery.summary: Returned failure inside transactional accept_registration rolls back source and owner consequences; scheduled job is not acceptance authority.
Lost response is reconciled via the same operation ID and immutable payload. Replay returns no bearer.
Tombstones preserve non-reuse, while unavailable old fingerprint keys/verifiers fail closed.

cases: Registration validation, exact replay, changed payload/password and tombstone/expiry refusal.
tests.proves: Executable focused primitive/replay coverage in repository.
tests.limits: Source inspected here; do not transfer historical run results to this map revision.

cases: Owner write set, rollback, concurrent acceptance and duplicate-email neutrality.
tests.proves: Actual Ash/PostgreSQL orchestration tests with independent connection race helpers.
tests.limits: No claim that JSON validation executes these tests or proves production delivery.

safe_extensions.summary: Extend registration through Identity.register/1 and the existing acceptance action; maintain rollback and replay tests when changing write set.
Use Communications and Audit owner interfaces for new consequences; inspect their current capability handoffs before extending.

reuse.summary: Reuse Identity.register/1 as caller interface and RegistrationBinding for immutable replay verification.
Reuse the existing database uniqueness and PMR reservation mechanisms; do not duplicate arbitration.

prohibited_shortcuts.summary: Do not call accept_new_registration or Account :register directly from delivery code to bypass owner validation/replay.
Do not introduce direct Repo/raw SQL/Ecto.Multi business writes, a second Account authority, or process-local uniqueness.
Do not equate MessageIntent, queued Audit work or verification_pending with email delivery, verified email or authenticated session.

proof_limitations: Descriptive source snapshot, subordinate to current governance and live Plane.
Schema/path/hash checks cannot establish the semantic truth of prose or declarations. Independent Master Gate must review claims against exact source/tests.
The historical P8-05 Markdown describes an older implementation snapshot; downstream Communications execution now has its own p8-10 handoff. This record covers registration acceptance only.
